definition: A job description is the written wording used to describe a job. In this context, its language can include or exclude social groups, shaping how welcomed, motivated, or targeted applicants expect to feel.

reasons: The packet does not define a job description as the written wording used to describe a job; it only refers to a job description in the context of gender-inclusive/exclusive language.

The added claim that the wording can include or exclude social groups is only partly supported; the packet supports gender-exclusive language affecting women, but not a general definition about social groups.
“Welcomed” and “targeted applicants expect to feel” are not supported by the packet; the packet mentions anticipated ostracism, perceived sexism, motivation, and identification instead.

The packet does not support the claim that a job description is “the written wording used to describe a job”; it only discusses job descriptions containing gender-inclusive vs. gender-exclusive language in relation to women’s responses.

The packet supports that gender-exclusive (vs. inclusive) language in job descriptions can be interpreted as exclusionary/sexist and can affect outcomes such as anticipated ostracism, perceived sexism, and lower motivation and identification, but it does not support the broader phrasing that the language “can include or exclude social groups” or that it specifically “shap[es] how welcomed, motivated, or targeted applicants expect to feel” as a general, standalone statement.
